findings.summary: New roster phase/sector calculations bypass the established saved floating-point boundary.
findings.evidence: sector_of performs direct floating classification and float-to-i32 conversion. roster_event uses floor and bool.then_some(value as i32): then_some eagerly evaluates the conversion even when a field is rejected. The raw phase is compared as f32 before any raw-word classification. These paths run outside scan_step's ScopedRounding/full-state boundary, and Engine model_callback supplies no enclosing FP guard. Fractional conversion can alter status; signaling malformed words can reach floating comparison/conversion before a named refusal.
findings.minimum_correction: Give these NEW roster operations the existing bounded saved/restored arithmetic boundary, or implement raw-word integer classification/truncation without FP effects. Validate signaling/nonfinite/domain words before floating use or conversion, and avoid an eagerly evaluated rejected conversion. Reuse the narrow existing FP/refusal seam for caller-state preservation and malformed words, not a new diagnostic programme.

findings.summary: Standing-key liveness/sector is validated only for Next, not for Offer or hit completion.
findings.evidence: The provider calls roster.next and validates a standing key only when the kernel decision is Next. ENTRY(nonexcluded) returning Offer and RESOLVED(hit) returning DoneHit do not inspect the supplied identity at all. An unknown, ended or other-sector key is therefore accepted in these actual protocol phases, contrary to the new named-refusal contract. New stale-key tests exercise only Next. BEGIN/END/reset also do not enforce the absence of a standing key.
findings.minimum_correction: Before deciding or serving a scan phase, validate the supplied standing key against the live roster/current sector for BOTH ENTRY and RESOLVED, including Offer and DoneHit paths. Require an empty standing-key place in phases that carry none, while preserving insert mobile-identity and remove-key domains. Add positive-first unknown/ended/misplaced/key-on-wrong-phase cases in existing provider tests. No corrupt-list native or new framework is needed.
